The starter is called Gary. Gary is older than the truck.

## Where Gary came from

Started 4 January 2023 in the flat in Levenshulme, from scratch: 50 g wholemeal rye and 50 g water in a 1 L Weck jar, stirred twice a day. Day 3 it went mad (that's the leuconostoc bacteria, false rise, not yeast). Day 5 to 8 dead flat and I nearly binned it. Day 11 it doubled in 8 hours on its own and has done ever since. Ignore anyone online who says 5 days.

## Feeding ratio

Maintenance is 1:5:5 by weight. 20 g Gary, 100 g flour, 100 g water. At 24°C he peaks at about 6 hours and roughly triples. At 1:2:2 he peaks at 3.5 hours, which I use on bake days when I need him sooner.

Discard goes in crackers or the bin. I don't feel bad about the bin.

## Flour

- 80% Shipton Mill No. 4 strong white, 20% Shipton Mill dark rye
- 16 kg sack of each, about £1.10/kg delivered
- tried 100% white for a month (Oct 2023), slower and runnier, went back to the rye mix
- Marriage's wholemeal works in a pinch, a bit more acid

## Temperature

This is the bit that matters more than the ratio. Gary lives in a proving box (Brød & Taylor, £180, Dec 2023) at 24°C. Below 20°C everything stretches out: in Feb 2024 the flat was 15°C for a week, peak took 11 hours and the bread was dense and properly acidic. Above 28°C he peaks fast then collapses and smells like nail varnish.

## Reading the jar

- rubber band at the level after feeding
- ready when it's 2.5 to 3 times the band, domed, big bubbles on the side, smells like yoghurt and green apples
- past peak: dome flattens, streaks down the glass, smell goes sharp
- float test is rubbish for rye-heavy starters, don't bother
- grey liquid on top (hooch) means hungry, pour it off and feed

## Fridge and revival

Truck shut for 3 weeks in Jan 2025. Fed 1:10:10 with stiff dough (50% water), lid on, fridge at 4°C. Back out on 27 Jan, two feeds at 1:5:5 and he was back to full rise in 30 hours. Fridge max I've done is 6 weeks, needed three feeds.

## Backup

Smeared 30 g thin on parchment in May 2024, dried for 2 days at room temp, crumbled into a jar. Two jars: one in my kitchen, one at mum's in Stockport. Revive with 10 g flakes + 20 g water + 20 g flour, should take 3 to 4 days.

## Truck use

- Friday focaccia: 12 trays, 800 g levain built Thursday night
- levain build 1:4:4 at 9pm, ready 7am at 21°C in the commissary
- the pizza dough on Saturdays gets 10% levain on top of yeast, details in [[Pizza dough hydration]]
- Jörg's Sunday rolls use him too ([[Brötchen am Sonntag]])

## Other starters

Tried a raisin-based one this year for a sweeter, milder levain, see [[Yeast water starter]]. Different beast. Rob reckons the sourdough is easier on his gut than supermarket bread, he wrote it up in [[Fiber and gut health]]. Not sure the science agrees but he eats it, so.
